title: Learning to change a habit
goal: Reconocer cómo la forma verbal cambia el significado después de ciertos verbos.
strategy: No memorices solo una lista. Compará la intención de acciones como stop doing y stop to do: ¿termina una actividad o se interrumpe otra para hacer algo?
passage: When I started studying in the evenings, I used to keep my phone beside my notebook. I enjoyed checking messages, but I found it difficult to concentrate. One day, I stopped reading to answer a call and never returned to the chapter. After that, I decided to leave the phone in another room. I stopped checking it during study sessions. At first, I missed seeing every notification. Now I am used to working without it. I still remember putting it away on the first evening because the silence felt unusual. I also remember to tell my family when I will be unavailable.
questions: What does “stopped reading to answer a call” mean?
The narrator ended phone calls permanently.
The narrator paused reading in order to answer.
The narrator could not remember the call.
To answer expresa la finalidad de interrumpir la lectura: dejó de leer para atender una llamada. No dice que haya abandonado las llamadas como hábito.
Which sentence describes an accustomed state now?
I used to keep my phone beside my notebook.
I am used to working without it.
I decided to leave the phone elsewhere.
Be used to + -ing expresa estar acostumbrado; used to + base describe hábito pasado.
task: Escribí una reflexión sobre un hábito de estudio. Incluí used to, be used to + -ing y un contraste entre remember doing y remember to do.
model: I used to study with the television on because I disliked silence. When I tried a quiet room, I noticed that I read more carefully. I remember finishing a difficult chapter without checking the time. Now I am used to studying in shorter sessions, although I still need breaks. Before I begin, I remember to close unrelated tabs and put a glass of water on the desk. These changes do not solve every problem, but they make it easier to start.
checklist: Diferencié hábito pasado de estar acostumbrado.
Mi elección de remember refleja memoria de un evento u obligación pendiente.
contrast: I am used to study at night.
I am used to studying at night.
En be used to, to es preposición y va seguida de -ing.
